_comment: Light WS1 - no printed key; answers DERIVED.

_excluded_figures.desc: Man + plane mirror, figure shows position X, distance y and a 5 m segment; geometry figure-dependent
Optics experiment: u-vs-v graph through origin at 45 deg, asks coordinates of point P on experimental curve
Broken mirror split by 1 cm, figure showing two principal-axis halves; midway image positions figure-dependent
Diagram: three rays of light passing through converging lens along vertical line; which statement is correct
Convex lens, 'object needed to be placed (see figure)' with marked positions on principal axis
All four options are ray-diagrams; asks which diagram is correct
Glass sphere figure: rays X->Y reach Z inside sphere; asks speed of rays that glass cannot be
All four options are ray-diagram pictures; asks which depicts correct image formation

1.reason: REVIEW: 'rate of change utmost' interpreted as largest difference in refractive index. Differences: P->Q=0.15, Q->R=0.99, R->S=0.82, S->P=0.02. Largest is Q->R, so B. Ambiguous wording.

6.reason: In a torch the bulb is at the focus of the concave reflector so reflected rays emerge as a parallel beam.

7.reason: Covering part of a lens still forms the full image (every part of lens images whole object) but with reduced brightness.

8.reason: A lens must be transparent and refract light; clay is opaque so it cannot be used to make a lens.

10.reason: The laws of reflection hold for all reflecting surfaces (plane and curved).

12.reason: A concave mirror gives a diminished (smaller) image only when the object is beyond C, i.e. at a distance greater than the radius of curvature.

13.reason: A concave mirror forms an erect (virtual, magnified) image only when the object is between pole and focus, i.e. less than the focal length (10 cm).

14.reason: Plane mirror image is as far behind as object is in front. Moving the mirror 2 cm toward the object moves the image by twice the mirror shift = 4 cm.

15.reason: In torches/searchlights/headlights the source is placed very near the focus so the concave reflector produces a near-parallel beam.

16.reason: n(air w.r.t water) = 1 / n(water w.r.t air) = 1/(4/3) = 3/4 = 0.75.

17.reason: Dispersion occurs because different wavelengths refract by different amounts (refractive index varies with wavelength).

18.reason: In a rectangular glass slab the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, so emergent angle e = incident angle i.

19.reason: At grazing incidence i=90 deg, sin i = 1, so sin r = 1/n and r = sin^-1(1/n) = the critical angle.

20.reason: Deviation by two mirrors = 360 - 2*theta = 200 => theta=80 deg. Number of images n = 360/theta - 1 = 4.5 - 1 = 3.5; take floor => 3 images.

23.reason: A concave mirror gives a real, inverted, highly diminished (point) image when the object is at infinity.

24.reason: REVIEW: relative index solvent/ice = 1.24 -> n_solvent = 1.24*1.31 = 1.6244, matches option B. Wording garbled.

25.reason: Each reflection loses some light, so image intensity decreases after each reflection and only a few images remain visible.

26.reason: Powers of lenses in contact add: P = P1 + P2.

27.reason: An erect (virtual, magnified) image from a concave mirror needs object inside the focus, so object distance (100 mm) < f, hence f > 100 mm and R = 2f > 200 mm.

30.reason: A ray through the centre of curvature strikes the mirror normally (along a radius), so angle of incidence = angle of reflection = 0 deg.

31.reason: Covering the upper half with black paper still forms the complete image (each part of the lens images the whole object) but reduces its brightness.

32.reason: A ray incident at right angles (normal incidence, i=0) to the boundary passes straight through without bending; it does not get refracted.

33.reason: For a prism-like slab with non-parallel surfaces, the ray deviates and the emergent angle e is greater than the incident angle i.

34.reason: No bending occurs at normal incidence: i = r = 0 deg.

35.reason: Light is slowest in the medium of highest refractive index; carbon disulphide (1.63) is highest, so light is slowest in it.

36.reason: Black absorbs all colours so it never reflects red; red cloth can look black when no red light falls on it.

37.reason: Smaller refraction angle means more bending toward normal i.e. denser medium. r1 < r2, so medium A bends light more and is denser than B.

38.reason: For a concave mirror with the object between C and F, the image is real and inverted (also magnified).

39.reason: A car rearview mirror is convex (virtual image, wide field). It is NOT concave, so 'concave in nature' is not a characteristic.

40.reason: A ray passing through the focus of a convex lens emerges parallel to the principal axis.

41.reason: Speed of light is maximum in the medium with the lowest refractive index; S has 1.31 (lowest), so light is fastest in S.

42.reason: For reading small print you need a magnifying convex lens of short focal length; a convex lens of focal length 5 cm gives the greatest magnification.

43.reason: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image; conventionally the object/image is described between pole and focus.

44.reason: A rear-view (convex) mirror always forms a diminished image, so its magnification is less than one.

45.reason: A concave mirror forms a real, enlarged image when the object is placed between F and C.

47.reason: For a distant object a concave mirror forms a real image on the same side as the object (where the screen is), while a convex lens forms it on the opposite side. So same side in case (i) but not case (ii).

48.reason: Focal length of a lens depends on the colour (wavelength) of light, the material (refractive index) and the radii of the surfaces - all of these.

50.reason: REVIEW: Eyes-to-mirror = 2 m, chart 0.5 m behind head so 2.5 m from mirror; image 2.5 m behind mirror; eyes-to-image = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5 (m). Options labelled in cm; choosing 4.5 (option C).

51.reason: Lateral displacement increases with the thickness of the glass slab.

52.reason: A focal length of -15 cm (negative) corresponds to a concave mirror and a concave lens; both concave.

53.reason: Sun's rays converge at the focus, so f = 15 cm. Image equal in size to object (m=1, real) occurs at the centre of curvature, u = R = 2f = 30 cm in front of the mirror.

54.reason: REVIEW: convex mirror R=4 m -> f=+2 m; u=-6 m. 1/v=1/f-1/u=1/2-1/6=1/3 => v=3 m behind mirror. Choosing B (3 m).

55.reason: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction, not total internal reflection. Looming, diamond sparkle and mirage all involve total internal reflection.

56.reason: Concave mirror, real inverted image m=-3 => v=3u. Object-image distance = v-u = 2u = 40 => u=20, v=60. 1/f=1/v+1/u=1/60+1/20=1/15 => f=15 cm.

57.reason: Man 10 m from mirror, image 10 m behind => man-image distance 20 m. To be 5 m from image he must be 2.5 m from mirror, so walk 10 - 2.5 = 7.5 m.

59.reason: In bifocal lenses for presbyopia the upper portion is a concave lens for distant vision and the lower portion is a convex lens for near (reading) vision.

62.reason: Light going from denser glass to rarer water bends away from the normal.

63.reason: REVIEW: garbled stem mixing lens/mirror; f=10, v=20 gives u=-20, but the printed options are inconsistent. Best-guess D; flag for review.

64.reason: Object within focus of a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image behind the mirror.

65.reason: The laws of reflection hold for all mirrors irrespective of their shape.

66.reason: Light passing from denser glass to rarer air bends away from the normal, so the angle of refraction is greater than the angle of incidence.

67.reason: A concave mirror forms a virtual (imaginary), erect, enlarged image only when the object is kept at a distance less than its focal length.

68.reason: A concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, magnified image when the object is between the pole and the principal focus.

69.reason: Rays parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from a concave mirror, pass through the focus.

70.reason: Bending is greatest in the optically densest medium (highest refractive index). Glycerine (~1.47) is densest among water, mustard oil, glycerine and kerosene, so light bends most in glycerine.

71.reason: Light travels fastest in the medium of lowest optical density (lowest refractive index); Z has 1.002 (lowest).

72.reason: In a convex mirror reflection takes place at the bulging-out (outer convex) surface.

73.reason: Angle of incidence from normal = 90 - 30 = 60 deg. Angle between incident and reflected ray = 2*60 = 120 deg.

74.reason: A convex mirror has a wide field of view and forms a diminished image, so a full-length image of a tall distant building can definitely be seen using a convex mirror.
